rubriker.title: WSTC 2026 European Stage begins in Tsaghkadzor
rubriker._rss_content: The European Continental Stage of the FIDE ISCF World Schools Team Championship has begun in Tsaghkadzor, Armenia, with 27 school teams from 25 countries competing for places in the December Grand Final. After two rounds, five teams remain on maximum match points, with Gymnasium No. 50 of Minsk leading on game points. The opening day also featured messages from the previous continental champions and an Armenian carpet-weaving workshop.

rubriker.title: World Schools Team Championship Begins in Armenia
rubriker._rss_content: The 2026 FIDE ISCF World Schools Team Championship brings together school teams from across Europe in Armenia for an eight-round competition combining international chess, teamwork and cultural exchange.

Behind the scenes in Samarkand: Inside the Expo
rubriker._rss_content: Arne Kähler sets off by golf cart from the entrance gate to the exhibition area at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. He shows the stands of WR Chess, DGT and ChessBase, while also passing the ChessBase India workspace, the food court and the souvenir shop. Arne then visits the press area and the game zone before meeting a special guest at the ChessBase stand - elite grandmaster Levon Aronian! | Photo: ChessBase

rubriker.title: Afghan Chess Players Detained After Returning From Olympiad, EL PAÍS Reports
rubriker._rss_content: According to EL PAÍS, three of four Afghan chess players who secretly traveled to compete in the 2026 Chess Olympiad have been detained in Kabul after returning home and face an uncertain fate under Taliban rule.

rubriker.title: Timur Turlov, noveno presidente de la FIDE
rubriker._rss_content: La elección de Timur Turlov como presidente de la FIDE para el periodo 2026-2030 reabre una cuestión histórica sobre la cronología de quienes han dirigido la federación internacional. Aunque la propia FIDE lo presenta como su octavo presidente, el artículo recupera el reconocimiento de Augusto De Muro y revisa los antecedentes institucionales de 1939 para plantear una reflexión sobre memoria, documentación y justicia histórica en el ajedrez. | Foto: Federación Internacional de Ajedrez (FIDE)
